### Observed differences

- In the later window, A36, A37, A42 and A43 each appear in every trace, about once per case; before, each appeared in only about 54 in 100 traces. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC005, OCC006]
- In the later window these four activities run much earlier in the trace: mean position about 0.40 of the trace length, against about 0.57–0.59 before. [POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009]
- Their order relative to A26 and A28 reversed: before, A26 preceded A36 in about 53 in 100 co-occurring traces and A28 preceded A36 in about 53 in 100; in the later window A36 precedes A26 in about 97 in 100 and A28 in about 97 in 100, and the same reversal holds for A37, A42 and A43 (about 97–99 in 100). [REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020]
- A25 now leads into this group: before, about 95 in 100 of A25's outgoing transitions went to A28; in the later window they go to A43 (about 29 in 100), A37 (about 25), A42 (about 25) and A36 (about 19). Correspondingly, the distance from A25 to A28 grew from one event position (about 97 in 100 cases before) to five positions (about 99 in 100 after), consistent with the four activities now lying between them. [DIR001, LAG001]
- The group now chains into A28 rather than A31: transitions from A36, A37, A42 and A43 to A31 (about 21–29 in 100 before) are replaced by transitions to A28 (about 20–29 in 100 after). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- A27 also became unconditional — about 48 in 100 traces before, every trace after, once per case — and A26 now routes to A27 in about 97 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, where before A27 (about 47 in 100) competed with the group activities (about 11–16 in 100 each). Before, A27 and A36 co-occurred in only about 2 in 100 traces; now they co-occur in all traces, with A36 before A27 in about 96 in 100. [OCC001, DIR002, REL006, REL013]
- A25 precedes the group and A27 in nearly all later-window traces (about 96–98 in 100), after co-occurring with them in every trace. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]
- Positions of the surrounding activities shifted consistently with four events now running before A28: A28's mean position moved from about 0.39 to 0.47, A26's from about 0.54 to 0.61, A31's from about 0.63 to 0.66, and A25's slightly earlier from about 0.36 to 0.34; A26 now reaches A31 two positions later in about 95 in 100 traces (A27 in between), where before the distance split between two positions (about 48 in 100, via A27) and five (about 51 in 100, via the four-activity group). [POS001, POS002, POS004, POS005, LAG006]
- A40's participation rose modestly, from about 45 in 100 traces to about 58 in 100. [OCC004]
- A few lag results about A31's distance to the group activities rest on only 1–3 observations in one window and carry little weight. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the group A36, A37, A42, A43 executes between A25 and A28 near the start of the trace, whereas before it executed after A26, and that both this group and A27 now run in every trace: before, a trace ran either A27 or the group after A26 (co-occurrence about 1–2 in 100), while in the later window every trace runs the group early and A27 after A26. The distinct differences — the group's participation and placement, A27's participation, and A40's participation — clearly exceed the roughly one item expected by chance in an unchanged process. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC005, OCC006, REL013, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001]

The placement aspect is shown directly by relational and positional evidence, not only by frequency shifts: the group's order versus A26 and A28 reverses (about 53 in 100 before to about 97–99 in 100 after, in the opposite direction), A25's successor changes from A28 to the group, the group's successor changes from A31 to A28, and the A25-to-A28 distance grows from one to five positions — matching the four activities now sitting in between. The occurrence, position, routing, co-occurrence and distance items all describe one underlying difference, not independent confirmations. [REL007, REL017, DIR001, DIR003, LAG001, POS004]

Limitations: each window is a 200-trace sample, so a shift in the mix of process variants — the group-first behaviour simply appearing in all later traces while absent from the earlier sample — remains a competing explanation the evidence cannot fully exclude, although the magnitude and consistency of the order reversals make pure sampling noise unlikely. The internal order of the four activities stays mixed in both windows, so no fixed sequence within the group can be inferred, and A40's modest participation increase is not accounted for by this hypothesis. [OCC004, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030]
